events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.77 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip ran 13.1 km against an 8.3 km optimal route, a deviation of 4.80 km, well over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is crossed and RD-2's refund matrix applies [F1][RD-1]. The one off-route segment is 09:07–09:14, 5.77 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 4.67 km [F3].

On the driver's chat message at 09:03 — “mind if I go round via Marina Boulevard?” — the rider never replied; the record holds exactly one message and it is the driver's [F7][F8]. Consent under RD-5 must be the rider's own message sent before or at the start of the segment, and a driver's later statement that there was “no objection” is a claim, not consent [F9][RD-5]. There is therefore no rider agreement to the reroute, and RD-3 is likewise not engaged: the rider named no stop or route [F7][RD-3]. The segment counts in full, with no exempt kilometres.

The replaced stretch did carry congestion — New Bridge Road was in speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:54–09:14, which spans the segment start, so a traffic reason exists on record and no driver violation arises from RD-4; but under RD-2 a traffic reason only reaches `no_action` where the rider was informed and agreed, and here she was neither [F10][RD-4][RD-2]. The uninformed reroute therefore yields a refund of the excess distance fare.

Amount: (4.80 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4097/km = $6.7666 → $6.77 [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; the multiplier was 1.0× so nothing turns on SURGE [F5][F6]. The refund equals the excess distance billed on the record.

Supporting records are complete: a timestamped single-message chat, full GPS distance/segment data and a metered fare breakdown [F8][F1][F3][F6]. The driver's two upheld route disputes in 90 days require the RD-6 account flag [F16][RD-6]. The chat, driver statement and complaint were read for threats, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegations and contain none [F7][F9].
